articles.title_orig: Live Updates: At Least 68 Killed in Train Crash in Spain, Officials Say
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: At Least 68 Killed in Train Crash in Spain, Officials Say
articles.content_orig:
Toledo, Spain 5:13 p.m. Oct. 28
A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another in Spain on Wednesday morning near the central city of Toledo, killing at least 68 people and injuring more than 50, officials said, in one of the deadliest train crashes in Spanish history.
The cause of the crash, which sent parts of both trains down a rural embankment, was not immediately clear. It was the second lethal crash this year involving the same two rail operators, and it was likely to deepen doubts about the security of Spain’s once-vaunted rail system.
In Spanish news reports, passengers described an awful impact that tossed people from a dining car, broke limbs and piled passengers atop one another. People crawled out of windows and lay in a nearby field, where local workers, who had heard the crash, rushed to help them with first aid kits and saw the first bodies.
The crash also came about a month ahead of national elections, and it had the potential to become an issue in an already bitter campaign about the competence of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s left-wing government.
Spain’s rail authority, the Adif, said the trains involved were a “Renfe train and another from the Iryo company,” both covering the route between Madrid, the capital, and the southern city of Seville. Renfe is the national rail provider.
Initial reports suggested that the Iryo train was stopped on the tracks, and that the Renfe train barreled into it. Local news outlets reported that there were 397 passengers aboard the Renfe train and about 150 aboard the Iryo train.
Trains from the same operators collided on a southern line in January, leaving 46 people dead.
Isaac Barrientos, a spokesman for the government’s transportation ministry, said on Wednesday that initial reports indicated two carriages of the Iryo train had derailed. He said all traffic on the Madrid-Andalusia route had been suspended until further notice. “We ask passengers holding tickets for travel on this high-speed line today not to go to the stations,” he said.
“Shocked by the serious train accident in Toledo,” Mr. Sánchez, whose office canceled all scheduled meetings, wrote on social media. “Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations. My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families.”
The conservative opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, quickly voiced his own concern as well.
“I am very concerned about the information we are receiving regarding another train accident,” he wrote on social media. “The priority now is to assist the victims and support their families. My full support goes to the emergency teams working on the ground.”
His Popular Party canceled all its campaign events around the country.
José Bautista contributed reporting from the scene of the crash.
When the crash happened, Yahadi Mohamed Maulud, 41, who lives in the nearby town of Yébenes, loaded his car with water bottles and rushed to help. “We found a massacre,” he said, describing torn limbs and a blood-covered woman searching for her brother. One of the first to arrive at the scene, he helped to move injured passengers and carry stretchers. Mr. Maulud said he often took the train himself to Madrid for business, but no more: “I’m never getting on that train again.”
So many people showed up at Madrid hospitals on Wednesday to donate blood for victims of the train crash that the authorities are asking citizens to wait until Thursday or the following days, when more donations will be needed.
“The response from the people of Madrid to the call for blood donations is overwhelming,” said Isabel Díaz Ayuso, Madrid’s regional president. “Thank you, everyone.”
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez spoke from the scene of the crash on Wednesday afternoon. “It’s not possible for a country like Spain to suffer two high-speed train accidents in one year,” he said, adding that while today’s accident and a fatal January crash on the same line seemed unrelated, Spanish rail’s security systems clearly needed to be reinforced.
“If there has been negligence, it will come to light,” he said. “If there have been failures in the safety system, we will respond with the utmost firmness.” Spain needs to understand “what is the origin of this tragedy,” he said.
Mr. Sánchez offered his condolences to the families of victims and thanked emergency workers. He also declared three days of official mourning, as he did after the January crash.
Emiliano García-Page, the president of the Castilla-La Mancha region, said the death toll from the crash had risen to 68. Twenty-four of those killed were on the Renfe train and the others were on the Iryo train, he said.
“Firefighters, with the help of cranes, are still working to determine whether there are more fatalities,” he said, “possibly beneath some of the carriages or among the twisted wreckage they have become.”
In the middle of fields of alfalfa and almond trees, a seemingly endless procession of ambulances, police cars and firetrucks drove in and out of the crash scene, as rescue helicopters flew low overhead. The trains seemed twisted together, a mass of mangled metal.
Dozens of Civil Guard officers, some wearing the white protective suits used by forensic investigators, were inspecting the scene and gathering evidence. Broken cables and fallen utility poles were scattered all around.
A group of Catholic priests walked out from the area where the trains were located. “We came to pray for the dead,” said the Rev. Luis Lucendo, 63, a vicar of Toledo and parish priest in Villacañas, a nearby town.
“One man told us that his wife had died, and I was able to make the sign of the cross over her,” Father Lucendo said. “They were going to spend the day in Córdoba, but this is where their journey ended.”
At least 64 people were killed in the train crash, the emergency services of Castilla-La Mancha said on Wednesday afternoon. The toll makes the accident one of the deadliest in the country’s history.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is traveling to Urda to offer support to first responders and express his support to the families of victims, his government said.
Spain’s Civil Guard said on social media that it had set up offices in Madrid, Seville, Córdoba and Toledo for family members of potential victims. The primary goal is to identify missing persons through the collection of DNA samples, the agency said.
The president of Castilla-La Mancha region, Emiliano García-Page, confirmed that at least 30 people had been killed in the train crash, a number that may rise. About 80 people were injured, 50 of them, according to Mr. García-Page, with severe injuries.
Blood donation groups in the area of the train crash are urging donors to come to hospitals in Toledo and Ciudad Real to “urgently replenish the reserves. Blood of all types will be needed.”
The fatal train crash near Toledo on Wednesday comes months after a deadly collision in southern Spain that involved the same carriers. In that accident, in January, 46 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz, in the country’s worst rail disaster since 2013.
The crash in January occurred when a train belonging to the private company Iryo derailed as it traveled toward Madrid. The train had been traveling north from Málaga when two of its rear cars fell into the opposite track. Seconds later, a southbound train operated by Spain’s national rail company, Renfe, slammed into the carriages .
The two trains were carrying hundreds of people when the collision occurred. An official report on what caused that accident is not yet available, but preliminary investigations pointed to a broken rail as the likely cause.
The accident shocked Spain and led to deep uncertainty about the safety of the country’s rail system, which contains the world’s second-longest high-speed rail network.
The deadly crash on Wednesday was the third in Spain this year. Days after

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Gains Meekly As Alphabet Rises Ahead Of Earnings (Live Coverage)
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Gains Meekly As Alphabet Rises Ahead Of Earnings (Live Coverage)
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Stellantis were up Wednesday as the European car giant's third-quarter results showed it was making progress with its 60 billion euro turnaround plan.
Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier.
The automaker's industrial free cash flow improved to negative 4 billion euros, up from negative 4.3 billion the year prior.
Stellantis on Wednesday also reconfirmed its 2026 guidance and target to achieve positive free cash flow next year, which is a main focus for investors.
"Q3 was soft, but consensus expectations were far lower. Key here is that '26 Guidance was maintained while other auto OEMs and suppliers are cutting on elevated costs," RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan said Wednesday in an investor note.
Stellantis stock rose roughly 9% Wednesday in Milan and was up by 12% in early trading in New York, but it remains sharply down since the beginning of the year.
Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa told investors Wednesday that the company is ahead of schedule on its turnaround plan, which was announced in May. He said Stellantis expects to exceed its previously announced cost-cutting efforts of 6 billion euros under the plan by 2028, including 2.4 billion euros to start 2027.
"We are very confident in reaffirming our '26 guidance. Those include '27 free cash flow positive," Filosa said Wednesday in response to concerns about the carmaker's ability to achieve its free cash flow target.
Stellantis' 2026 guidance includes a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin.
Stellantis' turnaround plan includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products.
Stellantis is targeting roughly 23% revenue growth, from 154 billion euros last year to 190 billion euros by 2030, with a 7% adjusted operating margin by then.
European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition.
Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz said its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country.
Earlier this month, Filosa told CNBC that European regulators need to do more to incentivize carmakers to manufacture vehicles in the region to fend off Chinese rivals.
Filosa called for regulation that "incentivizes, rewards, and protects the ones that are able to demonstrate that they design cars, engineer cars."

articles.title_orig: China's secretive space plane caught on camera in incredible new photo released by US military
articles.title_zh: China's secretive space plane caught on camera in incredible new photo released by US military
articles.content_orig:
US military says the restrictions on the electric vehicles at Kadena airbase also apply to delivery drivers and taxis
One of America’s biggest overseas military bases has banned vehicles made by the Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD over security concerns, the US military in Japan said on Tuesday.
The ban, which went into effect this week at Kadena airbase on the southern Japanese island of Okinawa , has fueled speculation that similar measures could be taken at other US military facilities as part of Washington’s crackdown on Chinese technology it suspects of being used to collect sensitive information.
“These vehicles present an unacceptable and unmitigable risk to our personnel and our mission,” Lieut Col Alli Stormer, a spokesperson for the US air force 18th Wing at Kadena, said in a statement.
The restrictions apply to all BYD vehicles, including privately owned cars, taxis and delivery vehicles, reports said, adding that security personnel stationed at the base’s gates had been instructed to block BYD vehicles and instruct drivers to turn around.
Kadena, the biggest US air force base east Asia, would be directly involved in responding to a crisis involving China , Russia or North Korea .
Its inventory includes the powerful Typhon missile system, which is said to be capable of firing Tomahawk missiles as far as 1,600km, putting parts of China and Russia within striking distance. Kadena also hosts fighter planes and aircraft used for mid-air refuelling, surveillance and reconnaissance, according to its website.
The move comes amid concerns of potential information leaks via vehicle-mounted technologies such as cameras, sensors and GPS devices, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency said.
American military officials have not identified a specific threat, but the ban is part of wider measures taken by the US and other western countries to restrict Chinese smart technology in vehicles, mobile phones and other devices they fear could be used to “spy” on their owners.
In June the Pentagon added BYD to a list of 188 Chinese firms it believes have ties to the country’s military, drawing a protest from Beijing. The blacklist also includes the automaker Nio, e-commerce firm Alibaba and internet company Baidu.
The US defence department banned the sale and use of smartphones from Chinese companies Huawei and ZTE at military bases worldwide in 2018, again citing security concerns.
China has imposed similar restrictions on US-made Tesla vehicles. In 2021, it barred them from some government compounds due to security concerns over ⁠cameras installed on the vehicles. Beijing removed that restriction in 2024 after Tesla won an endorsement from the country’s top auto industry association.
BYD, which has not immediately responded publicly to the Kadena ban, overtook Tesla as the world’s biggest seller of battery-electric vehicles in 2025.
It is now expanding overseas, including in the world’s fourth-biggest auto market, Japan , where in July it launched its Racco electric minicar in the hope that the small, cost-efficient vehicle would carve out a place in a market dominated by domestic brands.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Iran rejects "unacceptable" ideas as Qatari mediators say they presented new draft deal to Tehran
articles.content_orig:
Qatari mediators on Sunday handed Iran a new draft deal to end the war, the Reuters news agency reported, citing an official briefed on the negotiations.
Tehran is considering the proposal and set to respond by the end of the week, the agency reported Wednesday.
The source added that there were concerns in Tehran before the meeting on Sunday that Israel could resume its bombardment of Iran this week.
The cost of the Iran war has risen to an estimated $47 billion, according to an estimate from the U.S. military's Central Command obtained by CBS News Tuesday.
Like previous estimates, it does not include damage to U.S. military bases in the Middle East. The bulk of the cost, $29 billion, is for replacing expended munitions.
According to a report released by the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office in September, the Iran war could cost approximately $2 billion to $3 billion per month for as long as it continues.
Exit polls from Israel's major television networks project that a majority of Israelis voted against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in Tuesday's election, but his Likud party still emerged as the largest party among all the contenders. Neither bloc, Netanyahu or the opposition, has a clear majority.
While Netanyahu appears to have won fewer votes than his main challenger, according to the early exit polls, both candidates will likely struggle to cobble together a coalition.
One or the other would need to obtain majority support in Israel's 120-seat parliament, known as the Knesset, in order to form a government.
Israel's two Arab parties won more seats in parliament than in any previous election. That electoral success comes after what some Arab voters told CBS News was a difficult time for them in the country under the hard-right government of Netanyahu, prompting a historic turnout for the minority community.
Both Netanyahu and those opposing him have vowed not to form a government reliant on Arab parties, arguing it would endanger the country if they gain enough seats to influence Israel's engagement in its myriad conflicts. Arab citizens of Israel are around 20% of the population.

articles.title_orig: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
articles.title_zh: Israelis await final election results as Netanyahu rivals weigh joining forces with Arab parties
articles.content_orig:
Israel’s Arab-led parties are projected to win a record number of seats in the Israeli parliament, exit polls indicate, making them increasingly hard to ignore by the leading blocs.
“Probably the most important phenomenon of this election is the rise and the revival of the Arab vote,” Daniel Shek, a former Israeli ambassador, said. “The statement is clear: You cannot disregard such a large portion of the electorate in the calculations for Israeli politics.”
The latest projections from Tuesday’s voting showed that the Arab parties – the Joint List and Ra’am – could hold a record combined 17 seats in the 120-member Knesset.
So far, no clear winner has emerged as partial results give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc 54 seats and the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot 49.
While Arab parties might theoretically wield influence as the two main blocs fail to win majorities in the Knesset, they are not “kingmakers”, observers said, pointing to what amounts to a political veto that limits Arab parties’ ability to turn electoral gains into influence.
“This veto is rooted in a racist structure that regards the Arab citizen as illegitimate and as an unwanted partner,” Honaida Ghanam, director general of the Palestinian Forum for Israeli Studies in Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, told Al Jazeera, alluding to the resistance by the majority of Israeli parties to form any government with Arab-led lists.
Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have rejected the idea of partnering with them, citing a lack of shared values.
The numbers from exit poll projections thus far are looking clear: If Eisenkot’s bloc teams up with Arab parties, they could secure the 61 seats needed for a majority in parliament and depose Netanyahu.
According to The Times of Israel, the latest partial results would give a partnership between Eisenkot’s opposition alliance and Arab-led parties 66 seats.
According to Palestinian political analyst Ahmed Najar, the unwillingness by the opposition bloc to join forces is purely “ideological”.
“Eisenkot has imposed loyalty tests on Arab parties and ruled out relying on them even as the electoral arithmetic makes their support indispensable,” Najar told Al Jazeera.
Observers are divided on this.
According to Najar, a partnership with the Arab parties is not only feasible, it may be the only “realistic” route for Eisenkot to remove Netanyahu.
Omar Shaban, director of Palthink for Strategic Studies, pointed to the fact that Mansour Abbas, the leader of Ra’am, has already shown a willingness to join Eisenkot’s government if the Israeli candidate is elected, based on the condition that internal security matters will be handled by the Arab party.
Abbas has even appointed Jewish lawmaker Yoav Segalovitz to the number two spot on Ra’am’s electoral slate for the elections, Shaban explained.
Such a collaboration, if it came to fruition, could help foster better relations between Palestinian citizens and Jewish Israelis, he said.
Meanwhile, on Wednesday, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said his party is prepared to take responsibility for bringing Netanyahu’s far-right coalition down.
“The government has made the lives of every Arab citizen miserable,” Jabareen was quoted by the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper as saying.
His movement “will know how to leverage” its political strength to advance its values, he added.
Ahmad Tibi, also a Joint List leader, on Wednesday said the bloc was extending its hand to the opposition alliance to oust Netanyahu, according to Israeli media reports. It was far from clear, however, that the bloc would formally join a governing coalition.
A roadblock to such a partnership is the more “radical” elements in Israeli society that Eisenkot would have to face who “don’t want the Israeli government to be supported or dependent on Arab votes”, Shabaan said.
Najar said Eisenkot would also have to persuade his prospective partners, including Naftali Bennett from the Together alliance and Avigdor Liberman, who heads the Yisrael Beytenu party.
“Politically, however, it would require him and his prospective partners, particularly Bennett and Lieberman, to abandon the longstanding Zionist consensus that Palestinian citizens of Israel may vote but that the parties representing them are not legitimate partners in governing the country,” he said.
Ghanam outlined four possible outcomes: another election, an opposition minority government supported from outside by Arab parties, defections from the opposition to Netanyahu’s bloc or a national unity government.
“Beyond the arithmetic, the most telling result of this election is the resilience of Netanyahu’s camp, which has proven deeply entrenched and cohesive,” she added.
According to The Times of Israel, Eisenkot has said he would consider partnering with any party that recognises Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, endorses the values of the Declaration of Independence and commits to all Israelis performing national service.
He hasn’t, however, expressed whether Ra’am, with or without Jewish lawmaker Segalovitz, would meet those criteria, the outlet also reported.
Yes, there is precedent for such a move.
Most recently, after the 2021 elections, Ra’am emerged as a possible kingmaker, and its support was vital for the formation of the short-lived Bennett-Yair Lapid government at the time.
“Ra’am participated in the 2021-2022 coalition while Arab parties have previously supported governments from outside, most notably during the Rabin period,” Najar said, referring to Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, who served in the country’s top post in the 1970s and 1990s.
“The obstacle is, therefore, neither constitutional nor practical but ideological.”
Netanyahu said on Tuesday that a coalition with Arab-led parties to form a government would be “a shame and a disgrace”.
“It is forbidden – simply forbidden – to endanger Israel and to establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties,” he told supporters.
Bennett, meanwhile, who is currently in third place, has reversed course from the past: He has made clear that he now only wants “Zionist” parties in government and wants to exclude Arab parties.
By contrast, Yair Golan, leader of the centre-left Democrats party, which is part of the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot, has urged his allies to abandon their refusal to cooperate with Arab parties.
“We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” Golan wrote on X.
The reluctance of Jewish-led opposition parties to work with Arab parties “reveals the fundamentally racist structure of the Israeli political system”, Najar said.
“Jewish opposition leaders describe Netanyahu and the far right as an existential danger to democracy, yet many would apparently prefer Netanyahu to remain in power rather than share political power with Palestinian citizens of Israel,” he said.
Their objection is not only to a particular Arab party or programme but to the very idea that Palestinian representatives could possess genuine governing power, Najar added.
“A state cannot credibly call itself democratic when more than one-fifth of its citizens are permitted to vote but the representatives they elect are treated as inherently illegitimate,” he said.
Palestinian citizens of Israel, he pointed out, are accepted as voters when their participation serves the system but rejected as political actors when they seek the power to shape it, Najar added.
“This is not an accidental failure of Israeli democracy; it is the consequence of a system built to preserve Jewish political supremacy,” Najar said.
“If Eisenkot is serious about replacing Netanyahu, he must decide whether he is prepared to challenge that racist political order or remain confined by the same exclusionary logic that Netanyahu has spent years exploiting.”

articles.title_orig: U.S. cruise ship suspends 3-year around-the-world voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs
articles.title_zh: U.S. cruise ship suspends 3-year around-the-world voyage in Cambodia due to fuel costs
articles.content_orig:
The luxury MV Odyssey ship slated for a years-long voyage around the world suspends operations amid high fuel prices
A luxury cruise ship that had embarked on a years-long voyage around the world was forced to suspend its operations and leave passengers stranded in Cambodia because of high fuel prices.
The ship, known as the MV Odyssey, had been carrying 203 passengers, mostly Americans, along with 156 crew members, Cambodian officials told the Associated Press . The ship has a 650-passenger capacity.
The Florida-based operator of Villa Vie Odyssey, the company that operates the cruise line, said it was working with passengers on organizing “temporary living arrangements”. The cruise ship had begun its journey in Belfast in October 2024 for what was described as a “continuous voyage around the world”.
“Extraordinary increases in fuel costs have placed our current operating model under unsustainable financial pressure,” a statement on the company’s website said. “We are working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and temporary living arrangements, and are supporting residents, crew, and employees as we evaluate restructuring and recapitalization alternatives over the next 60 days.”
The ship is now docked at the Cambodian port of Sihanoukville on the Gulf of Thailand, with a departure date still unclear.
The price of fuel across the world has jumped since the start of the US war on Iran earlier this year. The ship’s operator said the monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 from $1,800.
The strait of Hormuz, which transports much of the world’s oil, has effectively been closed since 28 February, the beginning of the war. Oil prices climbed to above $117 a barrel this month.
One resident on the ship, Randy Cassingham, wrote in a blogpost that he only discovered the cruise route’s cancellation after a company official posted a note on a message board for the ship on Monday morning.
“It of course didn’t come from out of the blue: we’ve been well aware of problems,” Cassingham wrote. “It was a cascade of problems piling up on one another, from the business model to mistakes by management to the mentioned crisis in fuel cost and availability, and more.”
Pamela Reckamp, a 59-year-old resident of the ship, told NBC News that company officials on the ship had held a meeting last month where they asked cabin owners to help them raise $1m so the ship could depart Ha Long Bay, Vietnam.
“She said: ‘If we don’t get this money, we have about four days of the ship running,’” Reckamp said. “‘Then the lights will go off and the AC will go off.’”
Carol Larson, 69, lived on the ship for 18 months along with her sister, Crystal Lavering, 72, she told the Associated Press. Larson, who is from California, expressed hopes that the journey could still be salvaged because she said the decision to live at sea had improved her health.
Larson told the outlet that she bought her cabin for $120,000, paid in installments, with additional monthly maintenance fees under a program that offered her the option of living onboard the ship for up to 15 years.
Larson blamed Donald Trump for the problems facing the ship and the suspended journey, as the war on Iran caused fuel costs to rise significantly. Despite the issues, however, Larson said she did not regret her investment.
“Because it was a startup company, I believe that it was a risk,” she said. “From the very first day, I said to myself that if it lasts a year, I can walk away and feel like I got my money’s worth … I still feel that way. I feel blessed to have been part of the experiment of residential cruising.”

articles.title_orig: Nelson Peltz-led group offers to buy Wendy’s for $1.4B
articles.title_zh: Nelson Peltz-led group offers to buy Wendy’s for $1.4B
articles.content_orig:
A group of investors led by Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has offered $1.4 billion to buy Wendy's , according to a regulatory filing Wednesday.
The group has offered $7.35 per share in cash to take the burger chain private, paying a 20% premium to Tuesday's closing price. In addition to Trian, it includes investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, plus Flynn Group, one of Wendy's largest franchisees.
Wendy's shares spiked about 15% in morning trading following the offer. The Wall Street Journal first reported Peltz's proposal.
Wendy's did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC. Trian declined to comment beyond the filing.
The take-private deal offer comes after a tough two-year stretch for the burger chain. Wendy's stock has tumbled 65% over that period, including Wednesday's gains. For six straight quarters, the company has reported same-store sales declines.
Wendy's is scheduled to report its third-quarter earnings before the bell on Nov. 5.
Wendy's challenges have made the company a cheaper acquisition target for Peltz, whose history with the brand dates back to an activist campaign he led more than two decades ago.
Budget-conscious diners have been eating out less often, and Wendy's and its rivals have leaned into discounts to lure consumers into restaurants. Wendy's has also dealt with a revolving door of chief executives, who have had different ideas about turnaround strategies for the struggling chain.
"In our view, a take private makes sense as Wendy's turnaround is likely to be prolonged given the challenged state of the lower income consumer and soft state of the quick service burger category," TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles wrote in a note to clients on Wednesday.
In May, former Potbelly CEO Bob Wright joined Wendy's as its latest chief executive, after his former employer went private. In his first earnings conference call with analysts in August, he was candid about what he views as the chain's biggest issues, like muddled value offerings, inconsistent execution at its restaurants and too many one-off promotions.
Trian previously explored a takeover of Wendy's in 2022, but later decided against it. The firm and affiliated parties own a 16.25% stake in Wendy's, according to the regulatory filing, making them the company's largest shareholder.

articles.title_orig: Fed meeting live updates: No hike expected, but investors watching Warsh for what's next
articles.title_zh: Fed meeting live updates: No hike expected, but investors watching Warsh for what's next
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Reserve's interest rate decision Wednesday likely will be short on suspense, with markets expecting the central bank to stay on hold even with inflation tracking well above target.
Markets are pricing in less than a 10% chance that the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee follows up its quarter-percentage-point hike in September with another increase, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Assuming that sentiment is correct, it will leave the Fed's benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75% and 4% — and shift investor attention to Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh and whatever clues he chooses to provide in his post-meeting news conference.
Traders expect the Fed to follow up the October skip with a hike at its next meeting in December.
The Federal Reserve's decision to raise rates at its last meeting boosted borrowing costs, and the expectation that more rate increases are in the pipeline means consumers are unlikely to see much relief anytime soon. Those elevated borrowing costs are adding to existing affordability challenges, particularly for lower- and middle-income consumers.
As long as the Federal Reserve keeps rates at the current target range of 3.75% to 4%, consumers are unlikely to see much relief. Elevated borrowing costs are adding to existing affordability challenges, particularly for lower- and middle-income consumers.
Higher rates continue to affect credit cards, auto loans and mortgages. Credit card rates have climbed to their highest levels since late 2025, while 30-year mortgage rates have remained above 7%, making homeownership less affordable. Auto loan rates have also stayed near 7%, with even higher rates common in the used-car market.
One bright spot is savings. High-yield savings accounts continue to offer relatively strong returns compared with traditional bank accounts.
Some experts suggest consumers can ease budget pressures by paying down high-interest debt, negotiating better loan terms and taking advantage of higher yields on savings.
The Fed's big problem today is explaining why it's holding rates steady when the inflation rate has worsened since its last meeting – and several indicators suggest more bad numbers to come.
Start with tomorrow's PCE price index, the Fed's preferred inflation indicator. Both Wall Street and the Fed are able to use the CPI and PPI to pretty much peg the change in the PCE. The headline is expected to rise 0.5% for September , which will boost the year-over-year rate to 3.7% from 3.4%. The Fed could look past that, assuming it's driven by the continued rise in energy prices. But the core rate is seen rising 0.3%, raising the annual rate by a tenth to 3.1%.
What about the much-touted three-month annualized rate, which many doves have promoted as showing that inflation is under control? It fell to 2.05% last month, almost spot on with the Fed's 2% target. Time to cut, right? Not so fast. Model in a 0.3% rise in the core and the 3-month annualized rate shoots up to 2.7%. The Cleveland Fed's inflation nowcasting gauge sees core PCE in October running at 0.25%. Model that number in and the three-month annualized rate would rise to 3.24% in October. The takeaway: the gauge is so volatile that it serves as a poor guide for monetary policy.
The Cleveland Fed's trimmed mean, which removes extreme price changes from the CPI, has hovered between 2.6% and 2.7% for most of this year, showing little change. The Dallas Fed's trimmed mean has stood mostly alone in supporting a dovish take on inflation at 2.2%. It's worth noting, however, the Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan has herself cautioned that the measure may do too extreme a job of trimming away inflation.
Another problem the Fed faces: a seasonal pattern of inflation spiking up at the beginning of the year. Goldman Sachs sees inflation easing next year as pressures from tariffs, the AI buildout and energy abate. But it worries, "companies could take the opportunity provided by start-of-the-year price increases to pass along their higher costs, resulting in a larger 'January effect.' "
The danger of a hold today amid current inflationary pressures is that the Fed may need to do more in coming months. TD Securities writes: "It only takes one notably bad inflation report and/or a collection of strong labor market data for the market to start pricing larger odds of a 50bp rate increase in upcoming meetings."
Markets were taking a cautious approach ahead of the Fed rate decision, with major indexes mostly positive and Treasury yields also higher.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is up less than 100 points, while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were around the flatine.
In the fixed income market, the benchmark 10-year note added about 3.6 basis points to yield 5.03%, while the 2-year note added 3.7 basis points to 4.774%.
Since Kevin Warsh took over as Fed chairman in May, stocks have generally fallen on Fed meeting days, then posted gains the day after, according to DataTrek Research cofounder Nicholas Colas. The S&P 500 in particular has rallied at least 1% on the three post-meeting days of Warsh's tenure.
The Fed's decision Wednesday follows a string of reports indicating that inflation is reaccelerating.
September's consumer price index showed annual inflation ticked up to 3.7%, driven by higher energy costs. The CPI is currently on one of its longest streaks of annual readings above 2% on record.
The producer price index rose to 6.3% year over year in September. It was the steepest 12-month increase since 2022 for the index, which acts as a gauge of inflation on wholesalers.
The Fed won't get the latest from its preferred inflation reading, the personal consumption expenditures price index, until the September number is released Thursday morning. Wall Street economists use CPI and PPI use to estimate PCE, and they expect it to rise as well.
The Federal Reserve is following a different reaction function as it sets monetary policy, according to Stephen Miran, a former chair of the Council of Economic Advisers and governor at the central bank.
"There's a completely new reaction function in town," Miran said Tuesday on CNBC's "Squawk Box."
That new reaction function is "leading them to forecast additional hikes," said Miran, who's now senior strategist at Hudson Bay Capital.
Fed meeting minutes from the September gathering showed officials anticipated another increase , but did not signal when. Fed funds futures traders are anticipating the central bank holds rates steady on Wednesday before raising them in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Miran said inflation expectations in financial markets have been "cool as a cucumber" about hitting the Fed's inflation target. He said no one was willing to bet that the Fed was not committed to getting inflation to its 2% target.
Goldman Sachs economists think Fed watchers may be disappointed if they expect any major revelations from Warsh. The firm thinks the Fed has decided to take an every-other-meeting approach to hiking, and Warsh, who disdains providing forward guidance on policy, isn't likely to offer much new insight.
"We do not expect significant new information from the press conference," Goldman economist David Mericle said in a note. "The seemingly strong support for hiking every other meeting means there is likely a high bar to deviate from that plan through the end of the year, which should limit the impact of Fed communication for now."
Moreover, "even if the FOMC decides to change course in the future and wants to communicate this to markets, Warsh's decision not to hint at the slower pace at his September press conference suggests he might prefer to again leave that to others," Mericle added.
Warsh has some explaining to do when it comes to the difference between the Fed's stance in September and October, according to Michael Feroli, chief U.S. economist at JPMorgan Chase.

articles.title_zh: Fox News Takes Jaw-Dropping Ratings Hit
articles.content_orig:
Fox News is suffering a catastrophic drop in viewership, which has plunged to historic lows just before the midterm elections, according to new data.
Preliminary Nielsen ratings obtained by Status ahead of their official release show that the Trump-friendly juggernaut is on track to post its lowest-rated month in total day viewers since December 2023, averaging just 1.1 million total viewers throughout October 2026. However, last yearâs ratings were buoyed by huge stories, including the Gaza ceasefire and the hostage release.
Among the key 25-54 demographic coveted by advertisers, the outlet is headed for its lowest-rated month in a quarter-century, averaging a paltry 98,000 viewers. It places third in that group, and fifth among 18-49 demos.
The collapse represents a brutal 27 percent drop in total viewers and a 32 percent dive in the 25-54 demographic compared to last October.
Even early-morning institution âFox & Friendsâ marked its second straight month below 1 million total viewers.
Fox is still the only network to average over one million in total day viewers for October. But while the network still leads overall cable ratings ahead of sports broadcast giant ESPN, even despite the return of football, the sudden drop-off might signal a stark reality for Republicans heading into next Tuesdayâs vote.
With Donald Trumpâs approval ratings stuck near historic lows, conservative interest appears to be cratering right when party bosses need enthusiasm the most.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
The ratings slide extends straight into prime timeâthe crucial 8 p.m. to 11 p.m. block managed by network chief Suzanne Scott under executive chairman Rupert Murdoch.
Fox News is averaging 2 million total primetime viewers, representing a 28 percent drop from last year, while falling 36 percent in the key demographic down to 183,000 viewers. The figures confirm that even the networkâs marquee evening stars are failing to keep core Republican voters engaged.
Even early morning institution Fox & Friends âtraditionally a staple of Trumpâs personal daily viewing routineâmarked its second consecutive month below 1 million total viewers and under 100,000 in the key demographic.
October registered as the morning flagshipâs worst performance in overall viewers since July 2015, and its lowest in the 25-54 demographic since June 2001.
Meanwhile, competitor networks are capitalizing on the shift. Progressive rival MS NOW, which Trump despises, expanded its daytime audience by 16 percent to 588,000 total viewers compared to last year. CNN, which Trump also despises, registered a 3 percent bump up to 402,000 daytime viewers over the same timeframe.
The ratings collapse coincides with escalating tension between Trump and his long-preferred news outlet.
Trump publicly slammed Fox News on Truth Social for airing interviews with Democratic candidates like Michigan Senate contender Abdul El-Sayed, Kentucky Senate candidate Charles Booker, and Iowa gubernatorial nominee Rob Sand, complaining that Republican figures were getting âblurred outâ by the traditional media.
âFoxNews is spending far too much time putting on the OPPONENTS of Republican Party Candidates, people that love our Country, and have Great Policies and Ideas,â Trump posted, accusing the network of âtrying too hard to be Politically Correct.â
Trump also raged after Fox News briefly cut back on live coverage of his signature campaign rallies, encouraging supporters to switch to Right Side Broadcast News (RSBN), the far-right outlet launched by Trump enthusiast Joe Seales in 2015 to stream rallies uninterrupted.
Even the primetime slot, which includes network heavyweights like Sean Hannity, is failing to deliver.
Behind the scenes at network headquarters, insiders suggest the programming choices reflect audience fatigue. Speaking on condition of anonymity, a Fox host told CNN that directives come straight from executives, noting the internal consensus is simple: âTrump doesnât rate anymore.â
However, with polls poised to open in a matter of days, the network has begun to switch the president back on. It aired his Texas rally live on Tuesday.
Fox News has been asked to comment on the Nielsen data.

articles.title_orig: EU set to scrap ‘associate member’ offer for Canada
articles.title_zh: EU set to scrap ‘associate member’ offer for Canada
articles.content_orig:
BRUSSELS — EU countries have dropped the idea of offering Canada "associate member" status in the 27-member bloc, opting instead for softer language promising "ever closer association" ahead of a landmark EU-Canada summit, according to the latest version of the draft statement, seen by POLITICO.
A group of countries including Germany, Italy, Greece and France all objected to mentioning associate membership in a joint EU-Canada statement to be issued in Montreal, the diplomats said.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen had originally proposed "associate membership" for Canada in her State of the European Union speech in September, catching some EU countries off-guard.
A previous draft of the joint statement had read that the EU and Canada would "work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada Summit the concept of Associate Member that will reflect, through this even closer association, our common endeavour and cooperation towards our shared goals of prosperity, economic security and strategic autonomy."
In the final version, the text reads: "We will create an even closer association between Canada and the EU... and work to define by the 2027 EU-Canada Summit the concept of an ever closer association of Canada to the EU, short of full membership itself."
Later in the statement, the language changes from "even closer" to "ever closer."
The text still needs final approval. EU countries have a deadline of 6 p.m. to raise objections.

articles.title_orig: Bank of Canada raises key interest rate, says another hike possible
articles.title_zh: Bank of Canada raises key interest rate, says another hike possible
articles.content_orig:
This story is part of Mind Your Business, a weekly analysis of the biggest business stories emailed to subscribers on Monday mornings. If you haven't subscribed yet, you can do that by clicking here .
The Canadian economy is facing two very distinct problems right now.
On the one hand, inflation is high and rising. So far, at least, price increases have been contained to energy . Inflation ticked up to 3.1 per cent last month, but core measures (which strip out more volatile components) remained subdued .
But as we saw in the U.S., the containment doesn't hold forever — and once price increases spill over into other sectors, it can be tough to rein them back in.
On the other hand, the economy is weak. And we haven't even really started to get a measure of the impact of the latest tranche of tariffs.
Those two duelling crises pose a difficult riddle for the Bank of Canada.
Weak growth would usually prompt the central bank to cut interest rates to spur some economic growth. But rising inflation makes the bank want to raise rates to slow the economy and keep prices from increasing too quickly.
Two problems — with two solutions in complete contradiction to one another.
'We have to be realistic' about Canada-U.S. situation, Bank of Canada governor says
One by one, most of the major economic outfits in the country have switched their forecasts. Most now believe that on Wednesday the Bank of Canada will increase its key overnight lending rate.
They all lay out the economics of the matter, but as Frances Donald and Nathan Janzen from RBC Economics remind us, the bank is seeing this year's surge in inflation through the prism of the last surge — the pandemic shock of 2022 to 2023.
"The cautionary lessons of the post-pandemic inflation surge ... demonstrated how supply-side shocks and persistent cost pressures can overwhelm an economy surprisingly quickly," wrote Donald and Janzen in a note to clients last week .
So, most economists now believe the bank will increase rates, even though they don't all feel the bank should make such a move.
Donald and Janzen say a quarter-point increase won't materially move the needle on where they think the economy is headed. (They had, after all, built their forecast on the assumption that rates were going to rise next year.)
"Ultimately, the signal of a rate hike on Oct. 28 has a larger meaning we shouldn’t ignore: Central banks do not have the same patience for inflation they might have had in the past, and are willing to act pre-emptively to guard against it," they wrote.
Bond yields are soaring to multi-decade highs. What does that mean for Canadian consumers?
Sign up for Peter Armstrong's weekly newsletter here
If we could wave a magic wand, we would probably like the economic data this week to come in opposite order. We have the interest rate decision on Wednesday and GDP numbers on Friday.
GDP stalled in July (zero per cent growth) and the economy is expected to have grown by 0.1 per cent in August. But new tariffs kicked in that month, so the risks to the forecast remain firmly planted on the downside.
Uncertainty is the new ... everything.
The Canadian economy and the Canadian consumer have both proven themselves to be far more resilient than expected. But each new obstacle takes a fresh swipe out of the Canada's potential growth.
On the upside, we will also get an update on the Bank of Canada's forecasts this week. The Monetary Policy Report is the central bank's deep dive into where it sees the economy headed.

Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. The might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse .
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra , lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Basically, Tamagotchi meets ChatGPT. Another interesting experiment from Meta as it explores AI companions. Would you use this? 👀 📱 iOS: https://t.co/Z0mh1ggx9q 🤖 Android: https://t.co/isq6HnwoxE pic.twitter.com/4cuklTNB8v
Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18.
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
“Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.”
The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.
Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games , and Vibes, which let you quickly generate videos .
Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets .

articles.title_orig: Stellantis Confirms Guidance as Turnaround Progress Continues
articles.title_zh: Stellantis Confirms Guidance as Turnaround Progress Continues
articles.content_orig:
Shares of Stellantis were up Wednesday as the European car giant's third-quarter results showed it was making progress with its 60 billion euro turnaround plan.
Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier.
The automaker's industrial free cash flow improved to negative 4 billion euros, up from negative 4.3 billion the year prior.
Stellantis on Wednesday also reconfirmed its 2026 guidance and target to achieve positive free cash flow next year, which is a main focus for investors.
"Q3 was soft, but consensus expectations were far lower. Key here is that '26 Guidance was maintained while other auto OEMs and suppliers are cutting on elevated costs," RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan said Wednesday in an investor note.
Stellantis stock rose roughly 9% Wednesday in Milan and was up by 12% in early trading in New York, but it remains sharply down since the beginning of the year.
Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa told investors Wednesday that the company is ahead of schedule on its turnaround plan, which was announced in May. He said Stellantis expects to exceed its previously announced cost-cutting efforts of 6 billion euros under the plan by 2028, including 2.4 billion euros to start 2027.
"We are very confident in reaffirming our '26 guidance. Those include '27 free cash flow positive," Filosa said Wednesday in response to concerns about the carmaker's ability to achieve its free cash flow target.
Stellantis' 2026 guidance includes a mid-single-digit percentage increase in net revenue and a low-single-digit adjusted operating margin.
Stellantis' turnaround plan includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products.
Stellantis is targeting roughly 23% revenue growth, from 154 billion euros last year to 190 billion euros by 2030, with a 7% adjusted operating margin by then.
European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition.
Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz said its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country.
Earlier this month, Filosa told CNBC that European regulators need to do more to incentivize carmakers to manufacture vehicles in the region to fend off Chinese rivals.
Filosa called for regulation that "incentivizes, rewards, and protects the ones that are able to demonstrate that they design cars, engineer cars."

articles.title_orig: America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare
articles.title_zh: America's largest budget airline reports 71% jump in airfare
articles.content_orig:
Frontier Airlines reported a 71% increase in airfare in the third quarter as the country's largest budget airline tried to pass along an even bigger jump in jet fuel prices.
Frontier's fare revenue averaged $67.82 per passenger in the third quarter, compared with $39.74 last year. Including the budget airline's many fees, such as for checked and carry-on luggage, total revenue per passenger rose 30% on the year to $138.22.
Customers kept booking despite the higher prices. Frontier's passenger count rose 18% to more than 9.8 million people in the quarter. That's a difference of 1.5 million passengers from last year.
The company said demand remains strong, even at these higher prices, but Frontier still lost money. The airline widened its third-quarter loss to $104 million from a $77 million loss a year earlier. Its fuel bill soared 82% to $425 million.
Frontier forecast potential adjusted profit in the fourth quarter, saying it expects to post an adjusted loss of 15 cents per share to adjusted earnings of as much as 5 cents per share.
Carriers from Delta Air Lines to Frontier have said customers are mostly continuing to book flights despite higher fares, but that record jet fuel prices, their biggest cost after labor, are eroding profits.
Frontier shares were up about 6% in early trading Wednesday.
Frontier had eclipsed Spirit Airlines as the biggest discount carrier in the country even before that airline collapsed in May.

articles.title_orig: Mercedes-Benz to Offer Voluntary Buyouts for Support Staff as Market Worsens
articles.title_zh: Mercedes-Benz to Offer Voluntary Buyouts for Support Staff as Market Worsens
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Mercedes-Benz on Tuesday became the third big German carmaker to cut its outlook for the year on tough conditions in China, underlining the scale of the crisis facing the industry.
Citing difficulties in China -- the world's largest car market -- as well as higher material costs, core profit for 2026 is now expected to be on a par with the prior year's 5.8 billion euros ($6.5 billion), the company said.
It had previously foreseen an increase of at least 15 percent.
Profit margins at the core car business are now indicated at between two and three percent for the year, Mercedes-Benz said, down from the three to five percent previously.
Mercedes-Benz shares fell 4.2 percent after the cut. Volkswagen and BMW were both down a little over two percent.
BMW and Volkswagen have both already cut their guidance for the year as sluggish demand combined with cut-throat competition from Chinese local rivals such as BYD and Xiaomi have eaten into profits.
Mercedes-Benz's vehicle deliveries in China -- last year already at their lowest level since 2016 -- fell a further 29 percent in the nine months to end-September.
Being partially muscled out of China has led to painful adjustments for Germany's car industry, one of the country's largest employers.
Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius has urged German workers to work extra hours without pay at the same time as expanding the company's manufacturing footprint in Hungary, where he says costs are about 70 percent lower than in Germany.
Volkswagen plans to have cut 120,000 jobs globally by the end of the decade in what is the largest restructuring in automotive history, eclipsing the 50,000 jobs lost after the bankruptcy of General Motors in 2009.
Core profit for the third quarter came in at 1.77 billion euros, Mercedes-Benz said in preliminary results, and the profit margin at the cars business was 2.5 percent.
"Structural challenges show no sign of abating," Ingo Speich, head of sustainability and corporate governance at Mercedes-Benz shareholder Deka Investment, told AFP.
"The poor results highlight just how essential further cost-cutting measures –- as well as attractive new products –- are. Both must be implemented sooner rather than later."
Mercedes-Benz reports full third-quarter results on Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Meloni furious as Italian judge frees man accused of inciting violent protests
articles.title_zh: Meloni furious as Italian judge frees man accused of inciting violent protests
articles.content_orig:
Youssef Siher exercised his right to remain silent when questioned by preliminary investigations judge Tiziana Landoni in Milan’s San Vittore prison on Tuesday.
Investigations into the unrest that rocked the centre of the Lombard capital on 17 and 18 October are proceeding on two separate tracks: messages found by investigators in a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members, and the Milan prosecutor’s inquiry into Siher’s alleged role in organising and spreading content linked to the so-called 17 October Movement.
The Monza and Brianza Digos (General Investigations and Special Operations Division) began investigating after finding a message in a chat in which a user urged others not to put their balaclavas on straight away, to avoid being identified by police.
On 22 October, acting on a warrant from the Milan juvenile prosecutor’s office, investigators searched the home of the teenager believed to have written the message. They found a balaclava and an Under Armour T-shirt thought to have been stolen from a shop looted in Milan. A search of another minor turned up a second T-shirt of the same brand, also believed to have been taken during the looting.
But it was the first boy’s mobile phone that gave investigators their most significant lead, pointing them to a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members. The conversations referred to weapons, knives, smoke bombs and firecrackers, as well as plans to attack officers, snatch their weapons, damage police vehicles and set public buildings on fire.
Messages cited by investigators include “And we steal their weapons”, “Let’s grab one, beat him up and take his weapon” and “Hey guys, if we’re going to protest, let’s set fire to a government building”. Others urged people to get hold of knives, clubs and pepper spray, while some discussed stealing cars and targeting businesses, with references to a “Gucci robbery” and a McDonald’s.
The chats also mentioned further demonstrations planned for 24 October, which risked turning violent. The information gathered helped trigger a nationwide preventive operation.
On 24 October, around 150 personal and home searches were carried out in several Italian provinces, coordinated by the Central Directorate of Preventive Police and involving Digos units and Flying Squads from various cities. The main aim was to find illegally held weapons and ammunition.
In Brianza, the checks covered 32 people living in 16 municipalities, including Monza, Seregno, Giussano, Carate Brianza, Limbiate, Nova Milanese and Desio.
Officers seized folding and butterfly knives, a hatchet with “1312” engraved on its blade – a numerical code for the acronym ACAB (“All Cops Are B*****ds”) – knuckledusters, a telescopic baton, two blank-firing pistols missing their red safety caps, glass breakers, balaclavas and other items classed as offensive weapons.
Investigators are continuing to piece together the alleged conduct and identify anyone else responsible.
Siher was detained on 24 October and is accused of incitement to commit crimes, aggravated by terrorist intent, and of organised violence during public demonstrations. Prosecutors say he runs the social media channels of the 17 October Movement, which was set up after the clashes in central Milan.
Landoni must now decide whether to validate his detention and grant the request for him to be held in prison pending trial, submitted by chief prosecutor Marcello Viola and prosecutor Francesca Crupi, who attended the hearing. Prosecutors argue there is a risk he could flee or reoffend. A decision is expected by 28 October.
Siher is represented by lawyers Benedetto Ciccarone and Yasmina Abu Sharar, who deny he incited violence or terrorism and have asked for his release.

articles.title_orig: UK budget: Healey accepts smaller fiscal buffer after global shocks hit economy
articles.title_zh: UK budget: Healey accepts smaller fiscal buffer after global shocks hit economy
articles.content_orig:
The U.K.'s finance minister John Healey delivered his first fiscal budget on Wednesday, announcing funding for defense, AI initiatives and measures designed to ease cost-of-living pressures.
The Autumn Budget included dozens of measures aimed largely at easing rising costs for Britain's population, but Healey was careful not to risk the ire of markets, which responded broadly positively to his plans.
As a net energy importer, the U.K. is vulnerable to external energy shocks.
Inflation has risen sharply this year, with surging fuel costs driving the annual inflation rate to 3.5% in September. Markets expect the Bank of England to hike interest rates next month, while government borrowing costs have risen sharply this year.
The U.K. government, led by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, had promised to alleviate economic pressures ahead of the budget.
On Wednesday, Healey said he would deliver "breathing space" for families, saying the country needs "radical change on energy," and citing the inflationary impact of the U.S.-Iran war — a conflict he said "we did not want."
His measures included the removal of standing charges on household gas heating bills, the extension of a tax break on electricity for millions of households through July 2027, and £100 ($133) checks for those living in the four lowest local housing tax bands. This will cost £2.6 billion.
Healey said tariffs would be removed on over 100 grocery products, a policy announced before the budget was officially unveiled. Small business relief from business rates — a tax on commercial premises — would be extended to include more companies in the hospitality, retail and leisure sectors. Other measures included £15 million to provide books for children, funding aimed at reducing homelessness and support for people to purchase their first home.
The U.K.'s minimum wage will rise by 3.9%, while a planned cut to tax-free savings thresholds was canceled.
But Healey also pledged to bring down the welfare bill, pointing to reforms to pensions and sickness benefits.
But he said he would not "write off a million young people [or] see disabled people suffer the indignities of a system that has been found 'not fit for purpose.'"
The U.K.'s welfare bill, which reached 10.7% of UK GDP in 2024/25, has been a contentious issue in recent years. Previous finance minister Rachel Reeves watered down her own plans to cut welfare spending after a rebellion from lawmakers within her party.
Healey also announced investments in developing — and regulating — the U.K.'s artificial intelligence industry.
"Nowhere is the necessary role for the state clearer than in artificial intelligence," he said, as he announced hundreds of millions of pounds in funding for AI security and sovereignty.
He announced a "covenant" for data centers in the country, with "strict tests" they must meet: "To invest in local communities, create local jobs and protect local water supplies. In return, critical data centers will get the grid connections they need, and, where necessary, be allowed to build onsite generation while they wait," Healey said.
Healey also announced tax breaks for founders, including a reduced capital gains tax rate on gains of up to £10 million.
Cash would also be injected into various regional hubs, Healey said, to "unleash Britain's innovation power."
The budget also included £10 billion of additional economic and military support for Ukraine .
"Today we send a clear message to Moscow: Britain will stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes," he said. More funding would go to defense, he added, to ensure the country can meet its NATO spending commitments.
"At the Spending Review next year, I confirm that I will set out the details of how we will meet our NATO commitment to spend 3.5% of GDP on defense by 2035, with a target date for 3% in 2030," he said. "In this new era of threat, the demands on U.K. defense are rising."
Healey said his spending plans complied with the so-called fiscal rules set by his predecessor. Under those rules, the government's day-to-day spending must be funded by tax revenues rather than borrowing, and debt must be declining as a share of GDP.
Alongside the budget announcements on Wednesday, the U.K.'s Office for Budget Responsibility forecast that the government would have £15 billion of fiscal headroom by the 2029/30 financial year.
"Despite global challenges, this Budget puts us on track to eliminate the current budget deficit and get Britain's finances into the black within three years," Healey told lawmakers in parliament before unveiling the full details of his fiscal shake-up.
The OBR forecast on Wednesday that national debt as a share of GDP would rise slightly to 83.8% next year, before steadily declining until it reaches 81.7% of GDP by the 2032 financial year. It also raised its growth forecast for the U.K., saying it now expects the economy to expand by 1.2% this year, 1% in 2027 and 1.6% in 2028.
Yields on U.K. government bonds, known as gilts, fell as Healey spoke. By 1:50 p.m. in London (9.50 a.m. ET), the yield on the benchmark 10-year gilt was 2 basis points lower at 5.323%.
Sterling was marginally lower against the U.S. dollar, and 0.2% lower versus the euro .
Healey said Wednesday that he would raise revenue "from those who can afford to pay."
"No tax rises on wages or dividends," he said. "Cutting taxes for millions of families and businesses."
Banks, gambling businesses and vape shops would be taxed to help pay for the new measures, he announced.
Healey — who earlier this month called Britain's banks the "jewel" in the country's economic crown — said the bank surcharge would now be raised by 3%, bringing it to 6%.
Healey said the U.K.'s "world-leading banks" make a "huge contribution" to the country — and he was now asking them to fund the "breathing space" for Britain's households.
The temporary measure will be implemented in January and end 15 months later.
The scale of tax hikes was not as severe as some in the sector had feared, and shares in London-listed lenders moved higher on the announcement.
Shares in U.K. banks rose. Barclays were last seen 3.3% higher, while Lloyds Banking Group rose more than 2.6%. NatWest Group was up 2.5%.
JPMorgan Chase , whose CEO Jamie Dimon joined bankers lobbying against additional U.K. taxes last month, said in a statement that "to single out this industry for additional taxes again, one of the UK's biggest generators of growth and jobs, lacks principle."
"It also overlooks that the banking industry operates in a highly competitive global marketplace," a company spokesperson said.
Dimon has previously suggested it may rethink the multibillion-dollar buildout of its new headquarters in London's Canary Wharf financial district if the government is "hostile" to banks.
The company said on Wednesday that it is "committed" to the U.K.
— CNBC's Hugh Leask contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Wife ran after husband Philip Young ‘brought someone into bedroom’, court told
articles.title_zh: Wife ran after husband Philip Young ‘brought someone into bedroom’, court told
articles.content_orig:
A woman said she locked herself in a bathroom after realising her then-husband had allowed someone else in the bedroom while she was blindfolded and having sex, a jury has heard.
In a police interview played at Winchester Crown Court, Joanne Young said she was restrained when she felt a hand on her wrist which she believed did not belong to her now ex-husband Philip Young.
Joanne - who has waived her legal right to anonymity - said Young, who has admitted drugging and raping her, later apologised and told her he had invited someone to watch the couple have sex after browsing online forums.
Four men who Young is alleged to have recruited to abuse his wife at their home are now on trial.
Warning: This story contains distressing details
On the second day of the four men's trial, two police interviews with Joanne were played to the court.
During the first interview, dated 29 July 2024, Joanne said the incident when she hid in the bathroom had happened in February 2023 after a night out with friends.
She told police she could not "remember all of it", but said Young had come upstairs after she had gone to bed.
Joanne said she "woke up with a blindfold and restraints on" and loosened the restraint on her right hand and then the left. At that point, she said, she felt a hand grip her wrist.
She said Young - who she believed was at the end of the bed - said "get down" to someone as she tried to take her blindfold off.
Joanne said she then saw someone ducking at the end of the bed and she ran to the bathroom and locked the door.
"The bed is a really big bed. So to have someone on the end of the bed and the left was not possible… I knew immediately," she told police.
The jury heard the couple discussed the incident, with Joanne telling police it was the first time she had ever seen her then-husband cry.
Joanne said she asked Young if he had ever invited anyone to watch them have sex before, which he denied.
"It was so intrusive. I was so upset. He knows I would have never said yes to that," she told police.
Joanne told the officer: "I didn't know if I should stay in the relationship or get myself out of the situation."
She said she took the incident as a "one-off" and tried to "move on".
Asked by an officer if there was a discussion between Young and Joanne about having someone else in the relationship, she said: "There was a joke years ago, a bit of banter, where he said in the kitchen something like 'would you ever want to sleep with someone else?'.
"I said no, and he said 'as long as I can watch you'. We laughed it off but it was a no."
"It was never a part of our relationship. There'd never been a discussion. He never asked me what I wanted, it wasn't a conversation," she added.
On the day Young was arrested, Joanne said he admitted to her he had shared images of her online without her consent.
Joanne said it felt like a "kick in the stomach" and she was left in "shock and utter confusion".
She said: "How he could do that to me. How he could do something that's so intimate that's not allowed. How can he do it? How can you do that and think that was OK?"
The prosecution also read out statements from people who had been friends with Joanne and Young during their marriage.
Joanne's friend Susan said she thought the couple had a "dream relationship" before Joanne told her about the alleged incident of February 2023.
"She was in a real dark place about what happened," the statement said.
"After telling me, life went back to normal but what I witnessed from Jo was she didn't seem herself and that Phil had crossed a line from what he had done.
"Jo explained she was torn about why would Phil do this to her. She was in shock and seemed to be numb," it continued.
Emma Brown, who the court was told had been best friends with the couple since 2009, said Young "could handle his drink" and she "never saw him noticeably drunk".
"He was always on his mobile phone... I didn't know what he was doing as I didn't look at it," she added.
The four men jointly charged with Young, 50, are accused of the following offences:
Jurors were shown videos earlier which allegedly showed Sanderson-Doyle, Wilkins and Macksoni sexually assaulting Joanne.
Young, a former Conservative Swindon councillor, previously admitted 14 counts of voyeurism, 11 of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, seven of assault by penetration, four of sexual assault and one of publishing an obscene article.
He also published more than 500 intimate images and videos of his ex-wife and recorded her doing private acts for his own sexual gratification without her consent between 2010 and 2024.
A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.
Young and Hamilton will be sentenced at the end of the trial, which is expected to last up to four weeks.

Donald Trump Jr. enjoyed a secretive thirteen-person dinner in Europe with an eclectic mix of guests, including the Fyre Festival founder and a Miss World Estonia winner, according to the Financial Times .
On September 6, a private jet carrying the presidentâs son landed in Estonia for a one-day business visit that culminated in a private dinner at the offices of an online casino software company, followed by an after-party at a local cigar lounge.
The guest list featured a roster of eccentric American personalities, including former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale, Fyre Festival founder Billy McFarland, and former New York mobster Michael Franzese, who teamed up with Russian criminals in the 1980s to defraud the American government of millions of dollars.
Fyre Festival founder Billy McFarland, pictured on Fox News, was at the dinner.
Attendees at the subsequent after-party included celebrity poker players, an Estonian actress, and the reigning Miss World Estonia, 18-year-old Eliisa-Adele Toode, a recent high school graduate, the FT reported.
âEveryone involved who has factual knowledge is under a 55-page NDA, which is understandable given the guest list,â Craig Hilton, the eveningâs host and founder of Studioworks, told the Financial Times .

Despite the unorthodox crowd, the gathering also drew high-level establishment representation. Margus Tsahkna, Estoniaâs foreign minister, attended to discuss regional security, noting that the Baltic nation seeks a stronger U.S. and NATO military presence to deter potential Russian aggression following the invasion of Ukraine.

âIt was very interesting to meet someone whoâwhile not an active politicianâwields significant influence, and to see his attitude towards us,â Tsahkna said, adding that the meeting provided an opportunity to present national security visions to an influential figure within the presidential circle.
While Estoniaâs top diplomat was present, representatives for Donald Jr. maintained the trip was strictly private. A spokesperson emphasized that while he holds strong opinions, his views represent only himself and not his fatherâs government.

The European stop follows a series of unconventional overseas excursions. Earlier, Donald Jr. traveled to Mongolia for a two-day hunting trip in a remote camp alongside Umar Kremlev, a Russian oligarch and head of the International Boxing Association with close ties to the Kremlin.
Kremlev bankrolled a portion of Donald Jr. and Bettina Andersonâs Caribbean wedding celebrations, drawing bipartisan congressional scrutiny.
Following the Estonian meetings, Donald Jr. flew to Poland for another brief, highly guarded series of closed-door discussions.

articles.title_orig: Policeman kills knife attacker outside Israeli embassy in Serbia
articles.title_zh: Policeman kills knife attacker outside Israeli embassy in Serbia
articles.content_orig:
