articles.title_orig: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.title_zh: Two Nordic leaders urge Putin to end Ukraine war in rare direct contact by Europeans
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.
"We've not set out to speak on behalf of anyone other than ourselves," Støre said.
Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.
Zelensky later confirmed Stubb and Støre debriefed him after the call and said he was grateful for their "active support", while his Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the call had been "the right approach".
Finland and Norway, which border Russia, initiated the 90-minute call - held from Helsinki - to "discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe", the leaders' offices said.
Støre added: "The war comes with enormous human and material costs... The suffering and destruction will impact generations."
The Kremlin said Putin told the leaders that "a just and lasting peace" would only be possible if Russia's interests were considered.
Putin also reaffirmed to the Nordic leaders what he views as the "root causes" of the conflict - his frequent shorthand for Ukraine's desire to exist as a sovereign state.
"A fair long-term peace settlement is possible only if Russia's legal interests are taken into account fully and unconditionally", Putin said.
All three parties reportedly agreed to continue their direct phone communication.
There was no official EU reaction to the talks. The dialogue had not been coordinated with other European leaders, the Danish and Swedish prime ministers said. "I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," commented Sweden's Ulf Kristersson.
Meanwhile, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Stubb had informed him that Europe's position on the upcoming talks in the United Arab Emirates was "moderately optimistic".
Relations between the US and Ukraine and its European allies have soured since US President Donald Trump agreed to lift some sanctions from Russia, allowing Moscow to export oil to the America.
As the Trump administration's position on Russia has softened, several European leaders have said Europe should be trying to re-establish direct contacts with the Kremlin.
Stubb and Støre are the first European leaders to contact Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron's conversation with him in July 2025.
Soon after, Putin visited Alaska for a summit with Trump, and from then on Europeans were further sidelined from Ukraine peace talks. Moscow regularly mocks European leaders and accuses the EU of prolonging the war by supplying Ukraine with weapons.
But last weekend, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said having a European negotiator at the peace talks table would be "good".
And although he said Moscow did not view Finland and Norway as speaking on behalf of Europe, on Tuesday Peskov conceded that Stubb and Støre's talks with Putin had been "very constructive and practical talks with the leaders of two key neighbouring states."

articles.title_orig: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.title_zh: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
articles.content_orig:
Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’
Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’
Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with lines appearing on the right side of the display. On Monday, Apple acknowledged an “issue” and said it’s replacing damaged units, without going into much detail about how many broken phones have been reported so far.
So what’s actually going on?
Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed.
At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says.
You can see a visual representation of what Mokhtari is talking about in iFixit’s written and video Duo teardowns, which reveal where the hinge transitions, as the center hinge support makes space for a crossing flex cable, creating several edges that could ultimately be the culprit. The damage iFixit has been seeing is at a point where the center support bar might not always drop down far enough while the screen folds, possibly creating a stress “hot spot” between the flat bar and the bent screen inside a closed iPhone Duo.
At least one user with a broken Duo screen said they “felt something around the internal hinge” while showing it to a friend, kept opening it, and heard an “audible crack,” with the screen breaking. YouTuber CuriousHagi, who covered a Duo with dirt as part of a strenuous durability test, captured something similar on video , and the screen break appears in a similar spot. In a teardown video, CuriousHagi found that a part of the hinge that connects to the central bar had snapped .
Apple says the issue affects a “small number” of Duo units, and Mokhtari says that “In terms of numbers, we don’t know. Apple definitely has all the data here. And I suspect they know more than they’re telling us as well.” But he notes that because foldable screens are so delicate, a “certain number” of them will fail, as will a number of the hinges because they’re also “extremely complicated and delicate.” And while Apple isn’t recalling the Duos, “If three months from now, we’re still seeing the same kind of failure, then it’s a more widespread problem, and that might lead to a recall,” Mokhtari says.
Mokhtari points out that since this is the first generation of the iPhone Duo, it’s the first time Apple’s engineers are getting data on the hinge, and he says that “I guarantee you” Apple will redesign what’s at fault here for its next-generation foldable. He also notes that, generally speaking, “the phones do seem to be in people’s hands and people are using them, and they’re not running into any issues whatsoever.”

articles.title_orig: Taylor Farms recalls salad kits sold at H-E-B. See affected product
articles.title_zh: Taylor Farms recalls salad kits sold at H-E-B. See affected product
articles.content_orig:
Taylor Farms, the produce giant linked to the nation's largest-ever cyclospora outbreak that sickened more than 20,000 people this summer, has issued a new salad recall .
Taylor Farms of Dallas is recalling Backyard BBQ Chop Salad kits sold at H-E-B stores because they may contain allergens not properly listed on its packaging, according to an Oct. 27 notice from the Food and Drug Administration.
The recalled kits contain undeclared soy and tree nuts (almonds) that could trigger reactions in people with sensitivities or allergies. No adverse reactions have been reported to date.
Taylor Farms has been a consistent fixture in headlines this year after health officials identified iceberg lettuce grown by Taylor Farms de Mexico as the source of an unprecedented outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a gastrointenstinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis. The FDA declared the outbreak over in September and said on Oct. 2 that it had concluded its investigation, which found cyclospora was present in the environment where the lettuce was grown and processed. This latest recall is not related to cyclospora or Taylor Farms de Mexico.
The recalled kits were distributed at H-E-B stores in Texas and are packaged in a plastic bag. The product's best-by date and UPC are on the back of the package.
H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad Kit 13.4-ounce; UPC 041220300457, best-by Oct. 30, 2026.
Do not consume the recalled salad kits; either dispose of them or return them to the place of purchase for a refund, per the FDA notice.
Customers with questions may contact Taylor Farms at 855-455-0098.

articles.title_orig: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.title_zh: China’s top-secret spaceplane can’t hide in low-Earth orbit
articles.content_orig:
A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military’s X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.
The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.
Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. A US Space Force official revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference in South Korea, but the Pentagon did not release the full-resolution image to the public until Monday, when it appeared in an unclassified Defense Intelligence Agency assessment of threats to the United States in space.
The DIA report doesn’t reveal much new about what the Chinese spaceplane does in orbit. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020 with durations of up to nine months. The fourth mission is in orbit today after launching in February. It is not publicly known whether China has one or more such spaceplanes in its inventory.
The Space Force has two X-37Bs flying in rotation, with the longest of their eight missions to date running two-and-a-half years from launch until landing. US officials have released photos of the X-37B vehicles, published information about their design and dimensions, and disclosed a handful of experiments they have carried into orbit. Most of the X-37B’s activities in space are classified.
Like the X-37B, China’s spaceplane lifts off inside the payload shroud of a conventional rocket, then operates as a satellite once in orbit. The spaceplane flies like a miniature unpiloted version of NASA’s Space Shuttle and reenters the atmosphere for an autonomous land runway landing at the end of each mission. Ground teams then refurbish it for another flight.
The “enhanced maneuverability” of spaceplanes make them “more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” the DIA said in its report. So far, the Chinese spaceplane has only flown in low-Earth orbit (LEO) at an altitude of a few hundred miles. One of the Space Force’s X-37B flights soared to an altitude of more than 24,000 miles before using aerobraking to set up for reentry and landing .
Spaceplanes like China’s and the X-37B can also deploy small satellites from their cargo bay. Most recently, China demonstrated an ability to catch an object in orbit, perhaps using a robotic arm. The vehicle now in space released a sub-satellite in June and recaptured it in July, then did the same thing again in August and September, according to an analysis of open source orbital tracking data by Jonathan McDowell , an astrophysicist who catalogs spaceflight activity.
The official name of the Chinese spaceplane is even a mystery. It is often called Shenlong in Western publications, citing reports from the 2000s about China’s development of a robotic spaceplane. Chinese state media only refer to the vehicle as Chongfu Shiyong Shiyan Hangtian Qi, or CSSHQ, which means reusable experimental spacecraft, according to a fact sheet published by the Secure World Foundation .
The DIA did not disclose the exact circumstances of Maxar’s observation of the Chinese spaceplane, such as its timing, location, or distance, but Earth observations often use cameras to view other objects in space as their orbits intersect, an emerging field known as non-Earth imaging (NEI).
NEI allows commercial operators and government analysts to inspect satellites. This is especially useful for gleaning information about classified or proprietary satellite designs, extending a new avenue for international and corporate espionage to the high frontier.
The capability exhibited by Maxar and other commercial companies in the NEI field is distinct from the recent actions of some military spacecraft, such as Russia’s Kosmos 2612, which deliberately maneuvered to approach a US-registered radar imaging satellite earlier this month. Commercial NEI observations come from chance encounters, often at extremely high speed.
The DIA’s assessment of space threats includes an update on China’s pursuit of anti-satellite technology, or “counterspace” weapons. The intelligence agency reported the Chinese military likely considers directed-energy weapons (DEWs) “ideal counterspace systems” because they can be used to permanently or temporarily disable a satellite. One potential use for lasers in space would be to dazzle a sensor on an adversary’s satellite.
“China has multiple ground-based laser weapons with varying power levels to disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in LEO,” the DIA said. “By the late 2020s, China may field space-based directed energy systems and higher-powered ground-based directed energy systems capable of threatening satellites in higher orbits.”
The DIA noted China’s testing of ground-based anti-satellite missiles and the country’s historic demonstration last year of satellite refueling in geosynchronous orbit, a regime some 22,000 miles (36,000 kilometers) over the equator, something no other country has achieved above LEO. China has also tested a robotic arm that could snag a spacecraft out of orbit, and now operates a growing fleet of satellites called TJS that routinely approach foreign spacecraft.
The US Space Force also has a constellation of inspector satellites in geosynchronous orbit and recently procured more that could be refueled, overcoming maneuverability limitations. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed last month that the Pentagon has fielded weapons in space , making the United States the first nation to acknowledge possession of orbital weapons.
Russia is pursuing its own orbital combat program, which includes an ambition to deploy a nuclear weapon in space, according to US intelligence officials.
A more conventional Russian weapons system, known as Nivelir, is designed to fire projectiles from one satellite to smash into another. The Russian military simulated an attack using the Nivelir system in 2020. In April, Russia launched a fleet of small satellites into an orbit close to a commercial radar remote sensing satellite owned by ICEYE that provides reconnaissance imagery to Ukraine. One of the Russian satellites moved within “tens of meters” of the ICEYE satellite earlier this month before backing away, US officials said.

articles.content_orig:
Apple introduces :br(s):the new 14‑inch :br(s):MacBook Pro with M6
Supercharged by M6, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features incredible performance and next-level AI capabilities, enhanced connectivity, and up to 24 hours of battery life, delivering even more value
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 , delivering even more performance, powerful on-device AI capabilities, and faster connectivity for college students, business users, creators, and more. M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world’s fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. 1 The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power. 2 For those upgrading from M1, the performance gains are even more significant, with up to 11x faster graphics and up to 13x faster AI performance. 3 With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy. 4 In addition, the 14-inch MacBook Pro features Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, while superfast storage makes working with large files, exporting projects, and running demanding AI workflows fly. And with phenomenal battery life of up to 24 hours, it delivers the same remarkable performance whether plugged in or on battery, so users can work, create, and pursue their passions from anywhere. 3 It also offers the advanced features users love, including the stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with a nano-texture option, a 12MP Center Stage camera, an immersive six-speaker sound system, and a wide array of ports. Together with macOS 27, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is a major upgrade for existing Mac users and those coming to Mac for the first time. Available in space black and silver, it can be pre-ordered beginning tomorrow, October 28, with availability starting Friday, November 6.
“The 14-inch MacBook Pro is the pro laptop of choice for a wide range of users — from college students, to business professionals across every industry, to multidisciplinary creators doing it all on one device,” said Shelly Goldberg, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With the powerful M6 chip, we’re taking performance to the next level, with a boost in CPU speed and graphics and even more powerful capabilities for on-device AI. With its amazing battery life, remarkable Liquid Retina XDR display, and even faster connectivity, the new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers a fantastic combination of performance, capability, and value.”
M6: Blazing-Fast Performance and On-Device AI Capabilities
M6 brings even more performance and next-level AI capabilities to the 14-inch MacBook Pro. Featuring a powerful 12-core CPU, a 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and faster unified memory, MacBook Pro with M6 is faster and more responsive.
The 12-core CPU, with two more cores than before, brings blazing-fast single- and multithreaded performance, so users can fly through everything from multitasking across apps to compiling code to handling complex creative workflows. The 12-core GPU, also with two additional cores, delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics performance when compared to M5. 2 Everything from 3D modeling to photo editing and gaming feels incredibly fast, enhanced by a third-generation ray-tracing engine and Dynamic Caching to optimize on-chip memory. It also brings up to 25 percent faster performance for on-device AI workloads, like LLM prompt processing, compared to M5. 3 The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers up to 1.9x faster performance than M5 and works with the advanced GPU to dramatically accelerate AI workloads like image generation, Super Resolution, and AI upscaling. 2 The Neural Engine also powers Apple Intelligence, enabling advanced and energy-efficient on-device AI processing. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 does all this with industry-leading performance per watt and up to 24 hours of battery life, the longest ever in a Mac. With 16GB of unified memory standard, configurable up to 32GB, and higher memory bandwidth up to 170GB/s, MacBook Pro makes multitasking and working with demanding apps and large projects even faster.
The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 enables : 3
A Huge Upgrade with Even More Value
There’s never been a better time for customers to upgrade from a previous-generation MacBook Pro with Apple silicon or an Intel-based Mac. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 delivers remarkable value thanks to major performance improvements and powerful AI capabilities. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro also features all of the compelling capabilities that have made it so popular, including:
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 comes to life with macOS 27, which includes Siri AI, a profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal assistant; helpful Apple Intelligence features across everyday apps; and improvements that make the Mac even more responsive and reliable. Siri AI can draw on personal context to help users find what they need in the moment across messages, emails, photos, and more; answer questions about virtually any topic; and get things done across apps — all with groundbreaking privacy protections. Siri AI is integrated into Spotlight and systemwide context menus, and users can ask Siri about what’s on their display with Visual Intelligence using a dedicated keyboard shortcut. Users can also write and edit with Siri almost anywhere they type.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. In Safari, it powers new tools that automatically organize a user’s tabs into topics; notify them of website changes, like product restocks or price drops; and enable the creation of custom extensions based on a description. Users can also easily create an automation in Shortcuts by simply describing it, or tap into intelligent photo editing tools in the Photos app. The new 14-inch MacBook Pro gets even more responsive, reliable, and delightful with refinements to design, performance, search, and more. Updates to Liquid Glass deliver an even more focused and approachable experience. A new slider in Settings gives users the option to personalize Liquid Glass, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference, and app icons are sharper and more defined.
14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 and the Environment
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 45 percent recycled content overall, 6 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure, 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery, and, in a first for Apple, 100 percent recycled tantalum in multiple capacitors. It is manufactured with 60 percent renewable electricity, such as wind and solar, across the supply chain. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 7 and designed to be recycled.

articles.title_orig: China Is Treading Carefully in the Gulf. Here’s Why
articles.title_zh: China Is Treading Carefully in the Gulf. Here’s Why
articles.content_orig:
Choose your language to begin.
MBN Magazine · October 2026
Beijing is making the best of limited options.
Rana Sabbagh is an award-winning Jordanian investigative reporter and editor who has worked across the region for over 40 years. As editor of The Jordan Times, she was the first woman in the Levant to run a national daily.
For the second time this year, Saudi Arabia is under fire from Iran’s proxies, and for the second time China, the Gulf’s biggest oil customer, is watching from the sidelines.
Since Oct. 6, Yemen’s Houthis, allies of Iran, have launched the deadliest series of attacks on the Saudis since 2015. They say they are targeting what they call the kingdom’s most precious assets, the Aramco oil facilities and the airport in Riyadh.
The only ones that have come to its rescue are Britain and France. (The British have deployed Typhoon fighter jets, while the French have sent troops and air-defense equipment to protect critical infrastructure. Both countries have emphasized the strictly defensive nature of these moves.) Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under a mutual defense pact and rapidly deploy forces to the kingdom. The U.S. is providing intelligence and logistical support, but so far, has opted against putting boots on the ground.
And yet – even though it buys more Gulf crude than anyone else – Beijing has not played the role of guarantor in the ways that many analysts predicted. Its behavior follows the pattern it set during the roughly 40 days of open war between the United States and Iran that began on Feb. 28. In the weeks that followed, Iranian forces declared the Strait of Hormuz closed, and traffic largely halted until a two-week ceasefire was agreed on April 7. Iranian missiles and drones also struck Saudi Arabia and its neighbors.
When Iranian missiles were flying at Gulf capitals in the spring, Beijing was reluctant to mediate. Now that Houthi rockets are hitting Saudi Arabia’s strategic sites, killing at least 13 people at Riyadh’s main airport alone and injuring over 370, the Chinese are reacting the same way they did then: calling for calm, keeping their own tankers moving, and demurring from using their leverage to change the course of the war.
“China has its own calculations and a different strategic reading,” Mohammed Alsudairi, a lecturer in the politics and international relations of the Arabic-speaking world at the Australian National University, told me. The same dynamics applied to Iran are now applied to Yemen. “I see China’s ability to influence the reality on the ground as very limited,” Alsudairi, a specialist in China-Arab affairs, explained.
The boundaries of China’s influence lie in crisis management and de-escalation, not in rewriting Iran’s core security assessment.
China was not entirely absent in the spring. On March 31, it joined Pakistan in announcing a five-point proposal calling for a ceasefire and the resumption of normal navigation in Hormuz. Iranian officials said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei approved the April ceasefire after a last-minute nudge by China. But it was Pakistan, not China, that carried diplomacy forward.
When the truce unraveled, Beijing did not move to rescue it. A memorandum to end the war was signed on June 17, but the ceasefire collapsed a few weeks later after Iran attacked commercial vessels in Hormuz. By late July, Gulf capitals were openly testing the Chinese. A Reuters analysis at the time found Gulf Arab states looking to China, not Washington, to use its economic leverage over Iran to reopen Hormuz and the Red Sea. The answer was disappointing.
Beijing’s transactional understanding with the Houthis has largely kept Chinese-linked ships out of harm’s way but has not created pressure to end all attacks. “This war with the Houthis – and indeed since last year, with the exchange of fire between Iran and the Gulf states – has shown the limits of China’s ability, or really China’s willingness, to use its political capital to contain the war’s repercussions,” Alsudairi said.
If Chinese ships need safe passage through the Bab al-Mandab, as they did through Hormuz, Beijing can reach its own understanding with the Houthis and the Iranians, he said.
Alsudairi credits the 2023 Beijing Agreement , which restored Saudi-Iranian ties, with preventing something worse, because it opened channels of communication between Riyadh and Tehran. But he notes that fire was still exchanged despite that agreement. “China did not play the role of mediator, or at least of supporter of that agreement, as many of the parties analyzing it had expected,” he said.
He argued that Beijing came late to that deal too. Riyadh and Tehran arranged the agreement themselves over many rounds of talks. Any future accord, he said, would follow the same logic.
The parties would first settle what they agree on, then bring China in for their own political reasons, whether to improve ties with Beijing or to send a message to Washington. “There is a possibility that China plays a positive diplomatic role, but not as a mediator in the concrete sense,” Alsudairi said.
Dr. Wang Guangda, Secretary General of China-Arab Research Center on Reform and Development, put the limits more bluntly in response to my written questions. “China possesses constructive partnership influence with Iran on diplomatic and economic levels, but lacks coercive dominance,” Dr. Guangda said. In Beijing’s view, Hormuz is Tehran’s main counterweight to U.S. and Israeli military pressure, one that Iran will not give up for the sake of “the economic and trade interests of third parties.”
“The boundaries of China’s influence lie in crisis management and de-escalation, not in rewriting Iran’s core security assessment,” said Dr. Guangda, professor of international studies at Shanghai University.
The View Through Washington’s Eyes
During my recent visit to China, I interviewed two envoys, one Arab and the other Western. Both said that the country’s calculations in the Gulf start and end with the United States. They said that Beijing reads the war as an American attempt to impose security control over the region, with Washington firmly behind Israel.
The two diplomats I spoke to in Beijing, in addition to other political analysts, had the same view. “China does not want to be dragged into a military confrontation with the United States,” said the Arab envoy, who has spent over four years in China. “China has military bases, and they are not willing, for the sake of maintaining their foreign interests, to get into a confrontation with the U.S.”
The Western diplomat said the first casualty of any such confrontation would be Taiwan. Beijing intends to reunify the island with the mainland without force, and a push toward Taiwanese independence would be a strategic blow with domestic consequences.
Iran has also come up directly between the two leaders. The U.S. president has sought Beijing’s help pressuring Tehran towards a settlement, and the U.S. ambassador to China has said that Trump has made U.S. interests on Iran “very clear” to China (including in the latest summit meeting with Xi Jinping).
Alsudairi pointed to unconfirmed reports that Beijing scaled back intelligence cooperation with Iran after the Washington summit. He said that, true or not, the reports highlight the limits of the Chinese role.
The two diplomats in Beijing cited Latin America as the template for how far China will go to defend its interests abroad. Washington’s Dec. 2025 National Security Strategy placed the Western Hemisphere at the center of U.S. national security for the first time in decades, recasting China primarily as an economic competitor.
The document declares that the United States will remain the dominant power in the hemisphere, and that non-hemispheric actors, China foremost among them, will be denied military footholds and strategic resources there.
This is why Beijing made no major move to side with Iran. China cares abo

articles.title_orig: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.title_zh: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The Federal Reserve kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday as elevated inflation continues to pose a problem for central bankers who nevertheless seem reluctant to hike rates this month.
Fed watchers expect the central bank to keep benchmark rates in the 3.75% to 4% range , with bond traders pricing in a less than 10% chance of a hike on Wednesday, per CME Group. A rate hike in December appears far more likely, however, according to the Fed's dot plot and fed funds futures.
Although recent inflation data came in hotter than expected , several officials' remarks suggest the Fed will hold rates this month to continue assessing additional data. The proximity of the October meeting to the US midterm elections next Tuesday is also seen as a deterrent to bold monetary policy moves.
With the Fed holding rates steady seen as all but given, the focus is on what Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will say at his post-FOMC-meeting press conference on Wednesday. Warsh has deliberately avoided telegraphing future Fed policy moves, but hot inflation could elicit more insight from him into the path forward.
Federal Reserve interest rate changes on the eve of elections are tricky propositions, but for the third election in a row, the central bank may be unable to dodge that prospect after a hot inflation reading on Wednesday.
New Consumer Price Index data showed inflation heated up again in September , rising 3.7% annually and posting a 0.6% month-over-month surge. Core inflation, the measure more closely watched by the Fed, was also hotter than expected, rising 2.6% annually and 0.3% monthly. Following Wednesday's CPI release, odds of an October rate hike immediately spiked.
That new data comes as the next Federal Open Market Committee interest rate decision is scheduled for Oct. 28, just six days before Election Day.
"There is a political implication for going in October," Wolfe Research chief economist Stephanie Roth told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday, adding that committee members "would very much prefer not to do it," but the data is making a rate hike a distinct possibility.
"This makes the October meeting live," Roth said of the inflation reading.
Markets are heading into a busy few days for global central bank rate announcements.
Five major central banks are scheduled to make policy decisions this week, with two expected to hike and three to hold.
On Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand and the Bank of Canada will announce their decisions before the Fed releases its FOMC statement. Both central banks are expected to hike rates.
In Canada's case, the BOC is caught between a weakening economy and higher inflation. Governor Tiff Macklem has signaled in recent months that he is concerned about higher oil prices bleeding through to broader price inflation.
The next day, the European Central Bank is expected to hold rates steady, as is the Bank of Japan on Friday.
Many economists see the overall bias of central banks tilting toward tighter policy next year as artificial intelligence and the war in the Middle East drive inflation higher.
"If you're a central banker ... you've got to recognize this as a shock," Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said about AI at the IMF annual meeting this month.
The major US stock indexes rose on Tuesday as investors anticipated the Fed's decision on Wednesday.
The Dow ( ^DJI ) edged just above the flat line, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) gained 1.2% amid a semiconductor stock rally.
The US dollar index ( DX-Y.NYB ) rose above 102, and the 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ) remained steady at 4.99%. Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) also rose to above $80,600.
Conviction that the Fed would hold rates steady firmed on Tuesday, with traders expecting just 7% odds of a hike. Unless the Fed opts for a surprise hike, the decision is unlikely to move markets much.
But watch what happens to assets when Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh begins speaking tomorrow. Investors will be on alert for any hawkish signals.
The Federal Open Market Committee's two-day policy meeting has started and will conclude at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday.
The FOMC's decision on whether to cut, hold, or raise interest rates will be released at 2 p.m. tomorrow. Following that decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will hold a news conference at 2:30 p.m. that will be live-streamed.
This is the seventh FOMC meeting this year. The final Fed meeting of the year will take place from Dec. 8-9 and will include a Summary of Economic Projections, which will be used to gauge where policymakers see rates heading in 2027.
The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections.
Alan Blinder, a former Fed vice chair and a Princeton University economics professor, is expecting a "hawkish pause."
Although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh doesn't favor telegraphing the central bank's next move, Blinder said the moment calls for clarity.
"This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike."
The Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting kicked off this morning at 9:30 a.m. ET, as scheduled, a Fed spokesperson confirmed.
Expectations remain firm that the Fed will hold rates steady in a range of 3.75% to 4% after hiking by 25 basis points in September. Traders broadly view that the Fed will hike again in December.
But in October, there's a strong belief the Fed won't move rates. According to CME Group's FedWatch, traders see a 90% chance of no move.

articles.title_orig: Overseas Handler Linked to Iran Behind Foiled RAF Air Base Attack
articles.title_zh: Overseas Handler Linked to Iran Behind Foiled RAF Air Base Attack
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Two men were charged under the National Security Act on Tuesday over an incident last month at the RAF Fairford airbase , with prosecutors accusing a British national of trying to help Iranian intelligence in Britain.
RAF Fairford had been used by U.S. bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they were withdrawn on security grounds shortly after five British men were arrested outside the base in southwest England early Sept. 27.
The circumstances of the incident, which remain largely unexplained, attracted huge international attention, coming at a time of heightened concern about the security implications for Western states of the war between the United States and Iran.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said this month that the activity at RAF Fairford was likely to have been coordinated in Iran, which Tehran’s ambassador to Britain has denied.
British national Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, was charged with engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service between Aug. 31 and Sept. 28, with police saying the country is believed to be Iran.
Nouman Essghir, a 24-year-old dual British-Iranian national who was first arrested outside RAF Fairford on Sept. 27, was charged with one offense of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the U.K. on Aug. 22.
The pair will appear at London’s Westminster Magistrates’ Court later on Tuesday.
Police said that six other people, four of whom are British nationals who were arrested outside RAF Fairford on Sept. 27, remain on police bail.
The decision to bail suspects after an apparent major incident had drawn scrutiny, but on Tuesday police said that decision had helped secure charges against the two men.
“We know the decisions made during our investigations can sometimes appear illogical to those on the outside, but I want to make it very clear that there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them,” said Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K.
“In this case, this decision-making has led to swifter progress, better evidence and ultimately us securing the charges that I have announced today.”

articles.title_orig: UPS Stock Jumps After Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.title_zh: UPS Stock Jumps After Earnings Deliver Good News for the U.S. Economy
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_zh: Cheerios introduces a Ziploc-sealed cereal bag. Finally.
articles.content_orig:
The No. 1 cereal brand* and the No. 1 most trusted food storage brand** bring freshness you can reseal to the cereal aisle – available exclusively at Walmart.com beginning Oct. 27.
MINNEAPOLIS and RACINE, Wis. — Oct. 27, 2026 — You asked, Cheerios™ and Ziploc® Brand delivered – freshness you can reseal! After receiving hundreds of thousands of requests, comments and reactions annually on the topic, Cheerios and Ziploc® Brand have come together to introduce Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™. The new innovation features the first resealable bag inside a traditional cereal box, making it easier to pour, reseal and help keep cereal fresher longer.
The partnership brings together Cheerios, the No. 1 cereal brand*, with more than 50 years of Ziploc® Brand expertise helping people seal in freshness and store the foods they love. It’s a natural pairing for cereal lovers, 90% of whom say they already take extra steps beyond simply closing the cereal box to help preserve freshness*** like folding the bag, rolling it, clipping it or even transferring it to another container.
“General Mills has received letters, emails and DMs asking for an easier way to reseal a cereal box, and we decided it was time to partner with the ultimate freshness brand: Ziploc®,” said Emilie Knox, Vice President and Business Unit Director for Cheerios at General Mills. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ takes a small, everyday cereal frustration and finally gives consumers the simple solution they’ve been asking for, making the whole routine easier and more enjoyable.”
Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is made for how people want to pour a bowl of cereal, as well as store it. The resealable bag is designed to open only partially across the top to create a convenient “pour spout” as an easier way for the whole family to fill a bowl (or a cup, mug or even little hands). Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ then seals closed right inside the box for cereal freshness you can reseal.
“For generations, Ziploc® Brand has helped people keep the foods they love fresh through simple, trusted solutions,” said a Ziploc® Brand spokesperson. “Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is an exciting new expression of what Ziploc® Brand can do – bringing our resealable freshness expertise directly into the Cheerios package and Ziploc® Brand into the pantry in an entirely new way.”
Available as a new option in the cereal aisle for both Cheerios and Honey Nut Cheerios, Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ combines the same Cheerios families already reach for with Ziploc® Brand’s expertise in resealable storage, for an easier way to open, pour, reseal – and keep enjoying.
A fix that feels this intuitive was anything but simple. With nearly one box of Cheerios produced every second, the new Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ had to be developed to work at Cheerios scale while keeping the same familiar cereal flowing to pantries nationwide. For Ziploc® Brand, the partnership builds on a history of resealable storage that began with the introduction of its innovative zipper technology in 1968.
And there’s a fitting full-circle connection: Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is being produced exclusively in Buffalo, New York, in the same place where Cheerios was first made in 1941.
Cheerios with Ziploc PantrySeal™ is now available exclusively at Walmart.com and will roll out to retailers nationwide in the coming months.
For more information, visit Cheerios.com or follow @Cheerios on Instagram and TikTok . To learn more about Ziploc® Brand, follow @Ziploc on Instagram and @Ziploctheoriginal on TikTok.
* Nielsen Connect Total US xAOC Cereal Franchise $ Sales, L52wks 9/19/2026 ** Voted most trusted Food Storage Bags brand by American shoppers, 2026 BrandSpark® American Trust Study ***Suzy Survey, December 2025
General Mills makes food the world loves. The company is guided by its Accelerate strategy to boldly build its brands, relentlessly innovate, unleash its scale and stand for good. Its portfolio of beloved brands includes household names like Cheerios, Nature Valley, Blue Buffalo, Häagen-Dazs, Old El Paso, Pillsbury, Betty Crocker, Totino’s, Annie’s, Wanchai Ferry and more. General Mills generated fiscal 2026 net sales of U.S. $18 billion. In addition, the company’s share of non-consolidated joint venture net sales totaled U.S. $1 billion.
Ziploc ® Brand bags and containers provide smart, quality solutions that help you maximize your resources, and ultimately get more out of your everyday. From helping keep food fresh, to organizing knickknacks, to helping protect bulky items, Ziploc ® brand products are the food and home storage solution families trust. The Ziploc ® brand offers more than 20 products, available in grocery, mass merchandise and drug stores nationwide, including: Ziploc ® Freezer & Storage bags with Easy Open Tabs and Stay Open Design, Slider bags, Sandwich & Snack bags with Easy Guide™ seal, and Twist ‘N Loc Containers.
Founded in 1886 and headquartered in Racine, Wisconsin, USA, SC Johnson believes that a more sustainable, healthier and transparent world that inspires people and creates opportunities isn't just possible – it's our responsibility. A heritage of innovation and bold, transparent decisions is why our high-quality products and iconic brands – including OFF!®, Raid®, Glade®, Windex®, Scrubbing Bubbles®, Ziploc®, Mrs. Meyer’s Clean Day®, method®, Autan®, Baygon®, Mr Muscle®, Duck®, Lysoform® and more – are in homes, schools and businesses in virtually every country worldwide. As a global, purpose-led company, we are committed to making the world a better place today and for future generations. That means relentlessly bringing our expertise in science, innovation and partnerships to bear on some of the world's most pressing environmental and health issues like reducing plastic waste and eradicating malaria. Around the world, we use our resources to unlock greater economic and educational opportunities for people and communities where access may be limited, but curiosity and potential are limitless.

articles.title_zh: Quebec’s separatist leader threatens to play spoiler at Carney’s EU summit
articles.content_orig:
QUEBEC — Irritated over accusations of trying to muzzle Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that it was the Quebec premier’s decision not to attend a dinner organized as part of this week’s Canada-European Union summit.
“He was invited to the dinner; he refused,” Carney told reporters in Ottawa.
“We have had three consultations with the Quebec delegation about the European Union accord. It was his decision to leave the chair empty — again.”
The ruling comes as Hydro-Québec seeks to nearly double rates for large data centres, drawing opposition from companies including Google.
It is rather ironic that Quebec's separatist premier may have given us an idea of how to make Canada more Canadian.
